program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The binding contains an unresolved “(...)” and the node’s question/criteria are not represented in the supplied binding, so ensure the executable node is fully bound to the requested mug, headphones, edited image, and source-to-edit comparison. The traces repeatedly claim the mug is right of the headphones, but the edited image visibly contains two mugs: one left of/overlapping the headphones and another to their right, while the source has one mug. This makes object identity and whether the requested mug was moved ambiguous; do not treat the right-side mug alone as proof of completion or infer partial solely from the reference label. Add a criterion to track the source mug across the edit and assess its displacement relative to the headphones, distinguishing a moved original from a duplicated/new mug; use partial only when evidence shows progress that falls short, and unknown when identity/progress cannot be established. The five identical high-confidence traces are repeated judgments, not independent evidence. No transport or dependency failure is reported; the issue is visual grounding and criterion ambiguity.
